questions.stem: The summary note on foundations of Psychology: What a Person Is Told Before Agreeing sets out: "Potential risks and discomforts" Working from that claim, which must a beekeeper disclose in informed consent?

options.misconception: it leaves out risks the item explicitly includes

questions.explanation: Consent requires disclosure of risks and discomforts. Benefits alone, final results, or participant names are not required disclosures. At first glance tempting, "Only the benefits of participation" looks reasonable but does not hold up: it leaves out risks the item explicitly includes. A reasonable-sounding guess, "The names of other participants" is a seductive distractor: it confuses consent with confidentiality. Easy to pick on a quick read, "The final results in advance" fails on closer inspection: it confuses consent with debriefing.
